title: Emona founded
description: The Romans build the walled colony of Emona on the site of present-day Ljubljana.

title: Battle of the Frigidus
description: Emperor Theodosius I defeats the usurper Eugenius and briefly reunites the Roman Empire under one ruler.

title: Freising manuscripts
place: Freising, Germany (where the codex was kept)
description: Three religious texts are written down in an early form of Slovene, the oldest Slavic text in the Latin script.

title: Habsburgs acquire Carniola
description: The Habsburg dukes of Austria inherit Carniola and Carinthia and rule most of the Slovene lands until 1918.

title: Last enthronement on the Prince's Stone
description: Ernest the Iron is the last duke of Carinthia installed in the old ceremony conducted in Slovene by a peasant.

title: Counts of Celje die out
description: Ulrich II, the last Count of Celje, is killed and his lands, the only large rival domain in the Slovene lands, pass to the Habsburgs.

title: Slovene peasant revolt
description: About 80,000 peasants rise across the Slovene lands for their old rights and are defeated by mercenaries near Celje.

title: First book in Slovene
description: The Protestant reformer Primož Trubar prints a catechism and a primer, the first books in the Slovene language.

title: Dalmatin Bible
description: Jurij Dalmatin's translation of the whole Bible into Slovene is printed.

title: Glory of the Duchy of Carniola
description: Johann Weikhard von Valvasor publishes his fifteen-book description of Carniola.

title: First Slovene newspaper
description: The poet Valentin Vodnik begins publishing Lublanske novice, the first newspaper in Slovene.

title: Illyrian Provinces
description: Napoleon forms the Illyrian Provinces from lands taken from Austria, with Ljubljana as capital and Slovene used in schools.

title: Congress of Laibach
description: The rulers of Austria, Russia and Prussia meet in Ljubljana and approve Austrian intervention against the revolution in Naples.

title: United Slovenia programme
description: During the revolutions of 1848 Slovene intellectuals in Vienna and at home demand that all Slovene-speaking lands be joined in one autonomous unit with Slovene as its language.

title: First tabor at Ljutomer
description: Thousands gather at the first of a series of open-air mass meetings calling for a united Slovenia.

title: Ljubljana earthquake
description: An earthquake damages a tenth of the buildings in Ljubljana, which is then rebuilt as a modern city.

title: Maister secures Maribor
polity: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs
description: Slovene troops under Rudolf Maister disarm the German militia in Maribor, keeping the town and Lower Styria for the new South Slav state.

title: Carinthian plebiscite
description: Voters in southern Carinthia, many of them Slovene speakers, choose Austria over Yugoslavia and fix the northern border.

title: Treaty of Rapallo
description: Yugoslavia cedes the Slovene Littoral and Istria to Italy, leaving about a quarter of all Slovenes under Italian rule.

title: Liberation Front founded
description: Weeks after Germany, Italy and Hungary divide Slovenia between them, communists and other groups found the main resistance movement.

title: Kočevje Assembly
description: Delegates elected in Partisan-held territory meet as the first representative body of the Slovene resistance.

title: Kočevski Rog massacres
description: Yugoslav Partisans kill thousands of Slovene Home Guard prisoners and others handed back by the British after the war.

title: London Memorandum
description: The Free Territory of Trieste is divided, giving Yugoslavia the zone with Koper and Slovenia its outlet to the sea.

title: Trial of the Four
description: A military court tries Janez Janša and three others for leaking secrets, and the protests that follow start the Slovene Spring.

title: Independence referendum
description: Almost nine in ten of all eligible voters back an independent Slovenia.

title: Independence declared
description: Slovenia declares independence from Yugoslavia on the same day as Croatia.

title: Ten-Day War
description: The Yugoslav army moves against Slovenia and withdraws after ten days of fighting, leaving the country independent in fact.

title: Slovenia joins the European Union
description: Slovenia enters the European Union, a month after joining NATO, and adopts the euro in 2007.
